title: Short-range magnetic order and multi-stage phase transitions in the easy-plane van der Waals magnet CrCl$_3$
authors: T. B. Mazitov, M. I. Panin, A. S. Pakhomov, M. V. Bakhmetiev, E. O. Chiglintsev, A. I. Chernov, A. A. Katanin
abstract: We investigate the evolution of spin correlations and the nature of the multi-stage magnetic transition in the quasi-two-dimensional easy-plane van der Waals magnet $\rm CrCl_3$. By combining broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy and DC SQUID magnetometry on mechanically exfoliated micro-flakes with non-local dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) calculations, we analyze both long- and short range magnetic order in CrCl$_3$. Experimentally, SQUID and FMR measurements confirm the presence of the crossover to a spin polarized phase with the subsequent transition into an antiferromagnetic ground state upon cooling, but show robust short-range correlations at temperatures far above the magnetic ordering temperatures. Theoretically, we show the existence of highly stable local magnetic moments at room temperature, with a giant room temperature lifetime $τ$ of 130--300 ps due to a wide Mott bandgap. Below room temperature, a rapid growth of the in-plane correlation length $ξ$ signals the formation of strong short range magnetic order consistent with the experimental observations. We also obtain a temperature-driven crossover of the interlayer exchange interaction, which changes from positive (ferromagnetic) at high temperatures to negative (antiferromagnetic) in the low-temperature ordered phase.
summary: This work comprehensively investigates the complex magnetic phase diagram of CrCl3, a 2D van der Waals magnet. By combining SQUID/FMR experiments with DFT+DMFT theory, the authors map out multi-stage transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic states. The findings highlight the crucial role of persistent short-range correlations and temperature-dependent interlayer coupling in determining the material's magnetic behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the evolution of spin correlations and the nature of multi-stage magnetic transitions in the quasi-two-dimensional easy-plane van der Waals magnet CrCl3.
main_result: The research confirms a complex magnetic phase diagram involving crossover to a spin polarized (SP) phase followed by an antiferromagnetic (AFM) ground state, while theoretical work predicts robust short-range correlations persisting well above ordering temperatures.
method: The study combines experimental techniques like broadband FMR spectroscopy and DC SQUID magnetometry with advanced theoretical calculations using non-local Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DFT+DMFT).
model_or_system: The physical system is the van der Waals magnet CrCl3, which exhibits easy-plane XY anisotropy. The analysis focuses on the competition between intra-layer and inter-layer magnetic exchange interactions.
key_observables: Magnetization (M(T)), inverse susceptibility (1/χ(T)), resonant frequencies in FMR, and the magnetic correlation length ($\xi$).
important_parameters: Transition temperatures ($T_{SP} \approx 17 	ext{ K}$, $T_N \approx 14 	ext{ K}$), Weiss temperature ($	heta$), and exchange coupling strengths ($J_1$, $J_{\perp}$).
main_assumptions: The DFT calculations are noted to be performed without considering spin-orbit interaction, and the BKT formula is applied based on specific structural phases.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate SQUID magnetization curves showing magnetic transitions (cusps at 14 K), FMR intensity maps demonstrating mode evolution with temperature, and plots detailing the temperature dependence of exchange interactions and correlation lengths.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing experimental observations of multi-stage transitions using magnetometry and resonance. It then uses theoretical modeling (DFT+DMFT) to explain the persistence of short-range order and the temperature-driven crossover in interlayer coupling, culminating in a comprehensive magnetic phase diagram.
why_interesting: The interplay between strong electronic correlations (as modeled by DFT+DMFT) and emergent quantum phenomena like BKT transitions in low-dimensional magnets makes this highly relevant for understanding correlated electron systems beyond simple mean-field treatments.
